claims.context: Bibliographic facts from arXiv abstract page including submission history and license.
claims.text: arXiv:2609.02168 titled FUSE: An Evaluating Framework for Dangerous Capabilities of LLMs by Jin, Zhang, Chen, Liu, Lin, Huang, Liu, and Yang was submitted 2026-09-02 (v1) under cs.AI with CC BY 4.0.

claims.context: Framework design as stated in the paper abstract; full-text mechanics not verified from this abstract-only source.
claims.text: The authors present a modular framework evaluating each model through three orthogonal pipelines (Knowledge, Defense, Harm) under a unified protocol, aggregating into a standardized dangerous-capability profile with pluggable scenario seeds, knowledge banks, hazard queries, and judge rubrics; the chemical-biological instantiation is complemented by a cyber pilot demonstrating protocol transfer.

claims.context: Horizontal-comparison findings as stated in the abstract; underlying scores and model lists require full text.
claims.text: Instantiating with a chemical-biological module on 12 commercial LLMs from four families, the authors report sharply divergent K/D/H profiles: models with comparable knowledge differ in refusal resilience, strong defenders do not generate less harmful content when they comply, and family-level patterns separate Claude, DeepSeek, and GPT models.

claims.context: Temporal and reliability findings as stated in the abstract; trend and correlation statistics require full-text verification.
claims.text: Tracking K, D, and H against release dates, the authors report dangerous capability has not monotonically declined (newer models deepen knowledge while only partially improving defense), with reliability via cross-judge bootstrap rho above 0.79 for 4 of 5 judges and K-D-H inter-correlations rho in [0.32, 0.52].

claims.context: Primary official Kilo Blog retrieved 2026-09-17.
claims.text: Kilo announced on 2026-09-01 that Kilo for JetBrains, a native Kotlin plugin built for JetBrains split mode, now operates as a multi-agent control room for running parallel coding agents without leaving JetBrains.

claims.context: Parallel-worktree model and creation flows stated in the official announcement.
claims.text: Each task runs in its own isolated git worktree with its own branch, working directory, uncommitted changes, and session history; worktrees can be created from a base branch, an existing branch, or a pasted GitHub PR URL, managed in the Agent Manager, with a Continue in Worktree action for promoting exploratory sessions.

claims.context: Run, debug, and GitHub-context behaviors stated in the official announcement.
claims.text: Kilo adapts existing Run Configurations to the selected worktree, surfaces running processes plus Build/Rebuild in the Agent Manager, supports one-click full-frame debugging with frame reuse, and shows linked PR number/title/state with worktree-to-base comparison and separated uncommitted versus branch diffs plus file/line counts.
